name: Assyrian Neo-Aramaic
confidence_why: 4 independent first-hand sources agree (3 agree, 0 refine), none contradicts
catalog_quote: In Assyrian, stress is expiratory and normally is placed on the penultimate. It is not shifted in verb suffixation (i.e. is goes to the newly formed penultimate). Stress often affects the quality and length of vowels; it may cause the ommission of vowels and, at times, of entire syllables. (Tsereteli 1978)

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check: Maclean 1895 sect. 8 p.13 statement found verbatim in the scanned text we hold; Stoddard 1855:20 corroboration downloaded and confirmed; Noeldeke 1868 sect. 30 downloaded and agrees (second-hand from Stoddard); open-access NENA volumes we hold and Coghill 2020 give only family-level 'penultimate unless marked' notes. Every source seen agrees that default word stress is penultimate, so the penultimate stress is not in doubt and nothing suggests a reclassify of the position. The weakness is vintage and kind: the classification rests on a database entry (StressTyp2 < Tsereteli 1978, unverified) checked against an 1895 missionary reference grammar, while a 2016 four-volume reference grammar of the same dialect (Khan, Urmi) and a 1988 phonology monograph (Odisho) exist and are not yet obtained. Maclean's own sect. 8 (5)-(7) and Stoddard already record affix/enclitic-conditioned antepenult and some oxy
audit.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again: re-opened copies we hold. lines 2225-2290, running head 'ss 7, 8] ACCENT. 13': 'S 8. Accent.. In speaking the accent is almost invariably placed on the penul-|timate, even in foreign words.' -- verbatim as in the record's 'sources' text (record's quote/cite/loc fields are empty; the deciding text lives in 'sources' + 'the domain locator'). Same section, p.13-14, lists Exceptions (1)-(9): (1) vocatives accented on the first; (2) 'Words with the 3rd pl. pronominal affix.. are often accented on the last especially in U.'; (3) adverbs in -ait 'usually oxytone'; (4) a handful of lexical items initial-stressed
